seoTitle: How to Make a Brochure in Google Docs (2026 Guide)
metaDescription: Design a tri-fold brochure in Google Docs using landscape orientation, narrow margins, and a three-column grid for balanced, print-ready marketing handouts.
intro: A tri-fold brochure is a practical, low-cost marketing tool you can build entirely inside Google Docs. This guide covers rotating your page to landscape, tightening margins for more design space, and splitting your layout into a three-column grid so content lines up correctly with each physical fold.

steps.heading: Rotate to landscape orientation
steps.body: Open Page Setup and switch your document from Portrait to Landscape mode to match standard brochure dimensions.

steps.heading: Reduce your margins
steps.body: Set margins to a narrow quarter-inch or half-inch to maximize your available design canvas.

steps.heading: Create a three-column layout
steps.body: Use the Columns tool from the Format menu to split your document into an even three-column structure.

steps.heading: Insert column breaks
steps.body: Add Column Breaks to push headings, copy blocks, and imagery cleanly across the distinct panels of your brochure.

steps.heading: Add images and borders
steps.body: Upload photos and adjust layout boundaries within each column, then set up background borders to align front and back cover panels.

steps.heading: Check fold alignment before printing
steps.body: Run a print alignment check to make sure your printable text areas don't overlap with the physical folding seams of the paper.

faq.question: How many columns does a standard tri-fold brochure need?
faq.answer: A tri-fold brochure uses three columns to represent the front cover, inside panels, and back page of the physical fold.

faq.question: Why does my text overlap the fold lines when printed?
faq.answer: This usually happens when margins or column spacing don't account for the physical fold; adjusting your margins slightly wider near the fold seams can fix it.

faq.question: Can I use images across multiple columns?
faq.answer: Images generally work best contained within a single column to avoid distortion when the physical brochure is folded.

faq.question: Is a tri-fold brochure the same as a bi-fold?
faq.answer: No, a bi-fold uses only two panels, while a tri-fold requires the three-column setup described in this guide.
